The engineering know-how acquired by Dallara over 50+ years in motorsport represents a wealth of competences which extends far beyond the world of racing. Our extensive knowledge of composites, expertise in aerodynamics and excellence in designing lightweight, high-performance structures also finds application in special projects.

This new version maintains the versatility and comfort which made the original model famous, but introduces adjustable components such as the customizable backrest and anatomical handles, unique details designed to support athletes throughout their competition.

The project focused on the creation of critical components to improve aerodynamic performance: helmet, boot spoilers, and pole tips. Despite the limitations imposed by the rule book, Dallara’s technicians employed the same methodological rigor used for racing cars.

The first phase was an in-depth analysis of the athlete’s posture when competing, followed by an intense design phase. Each component was made to measure, taking into consideration the physical characteristics of the athlete and using the same technologies as for cars: from CAD systems to aerodynamic analysis, right through to construction of the final helmet made from carbon fiber.

The wind-tunnel testing phase represented a further challenge. Structures normally used for motorbikes were adapted to test Valentina’s equipment, with her demonstrating a remarkable ability to stay in position even with wind speeds of 130-140 km/h.

The Z-bike project is an extraordinary example of a special partnership between Dallara and Alex Zanardi, a friendship which transformed a personal challenge into a team victory.

A new challenge also came out of the collaboration between Alex and the Dallara team: to design and manufacture a commercial version of the Z-bike, accessible to all and suited to different kinds of disabilities.

Today, the Z-bike project continues to bring innovation to the adaptive mobility sector, and is available both for athletes with disabilities and for athletes without disabilities through the Z-bike brand (www.zetabike.it).

Dallara-AK Esports is an initiative born of Dallara’s decades of experience in simulations. A strategic partnership with AK Informatica which aims to redefine the standards of sim racing at a global level.

The partnership took its first steps in Indianapolis, a symbolic city in the motorsport landscape and a place with lots of history for Dallara, but then expanded with new centers in Paris, in the e-motion center, and at our headquarters in Varano, a town which now aims to become a landmark in the sim racing landscape as well.

This partnership brings together Dallara’s expertise in the simulation and virtualization of vehicles with the experience of AK Informatica in the e-sports sector, creating a solid, ambitious synergy which is unique in its field.

The Dallara Esports Championship, developed on Assetto Corsa, represents a concrete example of this fusion. The virtual competition is based on sophisticated mathematical models, derived from real data gathered on the track and in the wind tunnel, in particular for the Dallara Stradale and Stradale EXP.

The partnership with AK Informatica allowed these complex models to be transferred into an engaging virtual environment, offering participants the ability to race on historic tracks such as Mugello, Imola, and Spa.
To find out more about this partnership and the world of sim racing, visit the website: https://dallara-akesports.com/
Dallara’s partnership with Valentina Greggio, world champion speed skier, represents one of our company’s most interesting projects.

It was a request for help, motivated by the need to compete on equal footing with her international rivals – above all the French and Swedish – who could count on the support of their respective national industries to develop technically advanced equipment.

The project focused on the creation of critical components to improve aerodynamic performance: helmet, boot spoilers, and pole tips. Despite the limitations imposed by the rule book, Dallara’s technicians employed the same methodological rigor used for racing cars.

The wind-tunnel testing phase represented a further challenge. Structures normally used for motorbikes were adapted to test Valentina’s equipment, with her demonstrating a remarkable ability to stay in position even with wind speeds of 130-140 km/h.
Today, the relationship between Dallara and Valentina Greggio continues to evolve, in the constant search for improvement while balancing performance and safety.

Founder and company namesake Giampaolo Dallara established his own company in 1972 working out of his family home and garage. Fifty years later, Dallara celebrated its fiftieth anniversary. The Dallara story is compelling and the company is more active than ever.

Dallara’s location is no accident. In addition to being Mr. Dallara’s home town, Parma is located in the Emilia-Romagna region. Known as Motor Valley, the region is Italy’s racing and automotive heartland. Dallara’s neighbors include Ferrari, Lamborghini, Maserati, Ducati, Pagani and dozens of specialty suppliers.

When Maserati ran into financial problems and stopped racing, Dallara went to Lamborghini because Ferruccio Lamborghini wanted to race. Dallara played key engineering roles for the iconic Espada and Miura. Ironically, the success likely took Ferrucio Lamborghini’s attention away from racing.

Dallara left Lamborghini for de Tomaso and was finally able to design a Formula One car. Frank Williams raced a Dallara-designed de Tomaso 505/38 Formula One car in 1970. Fate intervened again when Ford bought a large stake in de Tomaso. Ford was already in open-wheel racing with Lotus, so they had no need for de Tomaso’s Formula One program.

Dallara’s motorsport credentials opened doors that grew the company. In addition to race car design that included cars like the Ferrari 333SP and Audi R8 LMP, road cars such as the Bugatti Chiron, Alfa Romeo 8C and Maserati MC20 are now part of Dallara’s portfolio.
